links.outcome: LLM referral and escalation advice across query urgency levels
links.effect: All 4 LLMs showed significant ordered trends (P<.001) with higher-urgency queries receiving more explicit referral advice; 97% (881/908) advised consulting a professional; DeepSeek-V3 only 74% explicit or urgent referrals versus 88-89% for others.
links.quote: All 4 LLMs demonstrated statistically significant ordered trends (all P<.001), with higher-urgency queries receiving more explicit referral advice.

links.outcome: Whether LLMs escalate appropriately to medical professional referral by urgency
links.effect: Urgency-responsive referrals in all models; 89%, 89%, 88% of Sonnet-4, Grok-3, GPT-4o responses were explicit or urgent referrals versus 74% for DeepSeek-V3.
links.quote: In contrast, DeepSeek-V3 showed a broader distribution, with 74% of responses falling into these categories.

screen.reason: Evaluates native LLM safety mechanisms (disclaimers and referral patterns) across different urgency levels of patient medical queries, but does not compare or test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
